about:
Setup

Shadow of the Tomb Raider, a captured clip, frame 39, both arms (crop). Output 4K, FSR Balanced (render 2258x1270). DLSS 5 neural rendering (small model) before upscaling, then 4.1.2l-lossy (FSR 4.1.2 Lite, our build). RX 7800 XT, Linux/Proton.

What to look at

Frame 39 is as found's oldest reused frame. Look beside both arms: a blue-gray band on the right, a dark copy beside the waist on the left; ours mostly removes both (left-arm crop: 32.40 vs 33.22 dB, ours closer).

What got worse

Whole frame 39 about equal (37.97 vs 38.03 dB); on the whole clip as found is slightly closer (38.91 vs 38.53 dB).

Rough max attainable fps on this GPU

Fps you can hold with every frame on time (no stutter), rough estimate: 2.1x
As found≈ 32 fps
Ours≈ 67 fps
Average fps is about the same (as found ≈ 69, ours ≈ 68): both do the same work, ours spreads it over every frame instead of one long frame in four.
Frame time, ms, four frames in a row (estimate; line = 16.7 ms, 60 fps):
As found31999
Ours15151515

Estimates: game + upscaler measured at 8.2 ms per frame without neural rendering; as found adds 22.9 ms on one frame in four and 0.7 ms on the others, ours 6.5 ms on every frame (both measured in the test harness at this size). Ours measured in the game's benchmark: 75 fps average, 68 minimum (one run). Average = from the mean frame time. Smooth = from the slowest frame type: the fps you can hold if every frame must be on time.

Notes

Frames from a captured game clip; display mapping is ours (x/(1+x), gamma 1/2.2), not the game's tone mapping; no UI or post-processing. DLSS 5 network run via the community AMD port (mauri870/DLSSNR-RDNA3); not affiliated with NVIDIA. Pictures: this project's local test harness, one run each (deterministic).
